title: routing policy specification compatibility gateway and schema validator
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Our current routing DSL accepts a mix of legacy keys (region, tier_priority, fallback_models) and newer declarative rule sets. This causes runtime surprises when configs rely on implicit tie-breakers and permissive fallbacks. Multiple production incidents (see INCIDENT-2026-02-11) traced to ambiguous region affinity rules and mismatched fallback variants.

Goal: Implement a "compatibility gateway" in the control plane that validates, normalizes, and lints routing configs at submission time. The gateway should: validate schema (strict), normalize legacy fields to the canonical DSL, surface deterministic warnings for ambiguous rules, offer a dry-run API to simulate resolution behavior, and produce telemetry suitable for migration dashboards. The runtime should still perform a lightweight safety check on loaded configs but not re-run heavy validation in the hot path.

Scope: - Schema validator for the canonical routing DSL (regions, tiers, model_variants, weights, capacity_constraints, fallbacks). - Compatibility translators for legacy top-level keys (region, preferred_tiers, fallback_models) and deprecated operator synonyms. - Dry-run / lint endpoint in the Console + CLI. - Controlled rollout: warn-only for two weeks, then block-on-submit for P1 configs. - End-to-end tests + property-based fuzzing for ambiguous resolution cases.
acceptance_criteria: Control-plane API rejects invalid schema submissions with clear error codes and suggested fixes
Legacy keys are automatically translated to canonical DSL when possible and annotated with warnings
Dry-run endpoint returns deterministic resolution trace (region chosen, tier step, fallback variant used) for sample requests
Console shows linter warnings and migration hints in the route editor
Telemetry events include: validation outcome, normalization actions, warnings produced, and sample resolution traces for 1% of requests
Runtime continues to use a small safety verifier that cannot block valid configs but flags runtime-only invariants
technical_decision: We will implement strict validation in the control plane at config submit time (synchronous path) and run expensive compatibility translations and linting there. To avoid increased request latency, the inference runtime will only run a compact verifier that checks for invariants required at runtime (e.g., no circular fallback, model_variant exists, tier capacity boundaries respected). This split minimizes performance impact on serving while giving strong guarantees before configuration ever reaches routing tables. We chose a warning-then-block rollout because a too-strict immediate block would break many existing customers; a long permissive period would prolong risk. The deterministic tie-breaker will be: explicit priority field > tier order > region affinity score > stable hash of route id. The gateway will annotate translated configs with a metadata header so we can trace original vs normalized shape in audits.
migration_plan: Phase 1 (week 0-2): Deploy schema validator to staging. Add translation layer for legacy keys in a warn-only mode. Enable Console dry-run UI in internal staging. Phase 2 (week 3): Canary deploy to 5% of tenants with warn-only submissions; collect telemetry and platform errors. Phase 3 (week 5): Convert high-confidence translations to automated rewrite (still warn), and block only obviously-broken schemas. Phase 4 (week 7): Block invalid submissions for all tenants and provide remediation docs/auto-fixes in Console. Phase 5 (post-block): Monitor runtime verifier alerts for 2 weeks; provide emergency rollback plan.
test_plan: Unit tests for schema validator covering all canonical fields (regions, tiers, weights, fallbacks)
Property-based fuzzing to find ambiguous fallback chains and priority inversion cases
End-to-end integration tests that submit legacy configs -> validate translation -> deploy to router simulator
Performance tests to ensure control-plane validation adds <50ms P50 to config submit path under normal load
Chaos test: simulate partially-applied migration where some routers have old cached configs and ensure deterministic resolution
rollout_plan: 1) Staging validation enabled for all routes; collect lint metrics. 2) Canary: enable for 5% of accounts (traffic and config submit) as warn-only for 2 weeks. 3) Expand canary to 25% with notify-to-owner on warnings. 4) After validation baseline confirms <0.5% critical warnings, switch to block-on-invalid for P1 configs. 5) Provide rollback scripts to remove validators at control-plane and re-enable legacy acceptance if severe regressions occur.
